course_title: Professional Practice and the Business Environment B
course_description:
Professional Practice is designed to give you the knowledge needed to effect change and implement design solutions in the real world. You will be able to identify barriers to technology uptake and work towards overcoming these through practical knowledge of: engineering economics, engineering law, engineering ethics, and the nature of engineering businesses. Students will learn how to undertake and interpret cost-benefit analyses, develop the skills required to understand business decision-making and economic drivers relevant to engineering and investigate key concepts required for ethical professional practice. Industry representatives and academics will deliver keynote lectures. Students will engage in workshops and project-based discipline-specific content and assessment which will lead the student through the issues encountered in professional engineering practice. Assessment will have both written and oral sections.

The course is structured around team-based, project-based learning. At the start of the semester, students will be directed into multi-disciplinary teams each of six students. Each team is tasked with developing an innovative start-up idea for a novel product or service. PBL applied class are structured so as to assist teams to develop a rigorous business case for their start-ups. The weekly workshop is used to deliver the tools and techniques that will be applied in weekly PBL sessions. UQ Ventures have been invited to present three guest lectures related to the Value Proposition Canvas, the Business Model Canvas and Pitching Start-ups. A representative of Engineers Australia will deliver a lecture on the ethical obligations of Professional Engineers.

course_aims: This course aims to equip engineering students with the knowledge and skills to navigate the complex factors influencing the successful delivery of engineering technologies and projects. It prepares students to identify and address technical, economic, regulatory, social, and environmental challenges, while assessing and managing risks and uncertainties. Through practical tools and strategies, students will learn to balance trade-offs and make informed business decisions. The course also fosters professional readiness by exploring organisational decision-making, financial project evaluation, stakeholder engagement, professional engineering expectations, sustainability, and the development of entrepreneurial ideas.

learning_outcomes.description: Develop a business case for a project (start-up), incorporating key aspects that influence critical decision-gates
Explain and critique your roles and responsibilities as a professional engineer working in projects
Perform a financial analysis of a project proposal
Identify, assess and treat strategic business risks
Critique the role of sustainability in business decision-making
Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team of engineers to create project proposals and evaluate project feasibility

assessment_details.task_description: Part A Start-up Value Proposition Your task is to develop a start-up pitch. You are restricted to a capital ask of no more than AUD $1m. Your start-up can be contained fully within Australia or can target other countries or regions, as long as the location aligns with the start-up idea. Your idea will ultimately be presented as a Pitch Presentation in Week 13 which will be targeted at your potential seed (angel) investors. Each team must submit a team charter and value proposition slide deck. Team Interviews on the Value Proposition will occur during the Applied Classes during Week 4. Supporting powerpoint should be submitted by 12:00 pm on the Monday of Week 4. Part B Financial Analysis & Business Model Canvas Considering a time line of 5 years, starting with 1 July 2026 (FY 27) as your timeline zero point up to FY31, and using an Excel™ DCF spreadsheet, construct a financial model for your start-up venture. Team Interviews on the Business Model Canvas will occur during the Applied Classes during Week 7. Supporting powerpoint should be submitted by 12:00 pm on the Monday of Week 7. Part C Stakeholder Sustainability and Risk Analysis Your task is to prepare a Stakeholder, Sustainability, and Risk Analysis evaluation for your start-up venture. This will be used to decide the next detailed development steps and where further study is needed. Team interviews on stakeholder, sustainability and risk will occur during the Applied Classes during Week 10. Supporting powerpoint should be submitted by 1:00 pm on Tuesday of Week 10. Part D Pitch report. A complete report covering all 3 sections of your project as a detailed report to your project manager. Due 12:00 pm on the Monday of Week 13. A PAF, limited in value between zero and a maximum of 1.1, will be applied. Part E The pitch summarises the business case around your start-up (Value Proposition, DCF Analysis and Stakeholder/Sustainability /Risk Analysis). A short proposal will be made to Angel Investors Pty Ltd, a venture capital company. The aim of the presentation is to convince an investor that your idea is worth investing in. In Class Pitch Presentation: Slides due by 12:00 pm on the Monday of Week 13. Presentations will occur during the Applied Classes during Week 13. Please refer to Blackboard for a detailed marking criteria. If, for whatever reason, you find that your group is not functioning effectively, please contact your Course Coordinator for support. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submission is via turn-it-in on Blackboard Ultra.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Extensions are not available for Parts A, B, C and E of this assessment item.
This is to allow the Team Interviews to proceed as scheduled with the marking team, and is consistent with professional and industry expectations.
For Part D (Pitch report), extensions are limited to 7 days as feedback will be provided within 14 days.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
